newsitem.title: CYPRUS: U.N. envoy starts new Cyprus mission.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy starts new Cyprus mission.

text.p: U.N. special representative for Cyprus Han Sung-joo of South Korea kicked off a new round of contacts on the divided island on Thursday with an hour-long meeting with President Glafcos Clerides.
During his week-long visit Han is due to discuss preparations for face-to-face talks between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities.
He handed to Clerides a letter from United Nations Secretary-General Kofi Annan and will later on Thursday give a similar letter to Rauf Denktash, the leader of the Turkish Cypriot community.
"The letter conveyed the very strong interest and concern of the secretary-general on the Cyprus issue and his determination to find a solution," Han told reporters.
The U.N. envoy avoided going into specifics about what he discussed with Clerides, the first of several meetings scheduled.
But he reiterated that there was a "window of opportunity" for face-to-face discussions between the two leaders which could pave the way for a political settlement.
"The window is there," he said. "It is not a very large one... we have to be very careful it doesn't get stuck so the job is to open it."
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops invaded the north of the island in response to a coup in Nicosia engineered by the junta then ruling Greece.

A Turkish Cypriot state proclaimed there in 1983 is recognised only by Ankara, which has 30,000 troops stationed in the north. U.N. attempts spanning decades to reunite Cyprus under a federal system have failed.

Tensions between the two sides have risen in recent weeks after the Cyprus government announced plans to buy anti-aircraft missiles from Russia, and Turkey said it would take whatever action was needed to ensure they were not deployed.
